did_you_know.text: The conflict between the men of Ephraim and Jephthah began when Ephraim complained that they had not been invited to join the war against the Ammonites, and even threatened to burn down Jephthah’s house.
Jephthah claimed that the men of Ephraim had not helped him when he called them to fight the Ammonites.
After the confrontation, the men of Gilead fought against Ephraim, and the text says that the men of Ephraim called the Gileadites fugitives living within Ephraim and Manasseh.
The men of Gilead seized the fords of the Jordan—the river crossings—to prevent the men of Ephraim from escaping.

The men of Gilead used the pronunciation of the word “Shibboleth” to identify the Ephraimites: anyone who said “Sibboleth” was identified as an Ephraimite. According to the text, forty-two thousand Ephraimites fell at that time.
Jephthah judged Israel for six years, and after his death he was buried in the cities of Gilead.

Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel for seven years. The text says that he had thirty sons and thirty daughters, and that he married off his daughters outside his family and brought in wives from outside the family for his sons.
Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel for ten years, and after his death he was buried at Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkeys; he judged Israel for eight years.
Abdon was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekite.
